review_method: EXTERNAL cross-review completed. Stage 2 (Bias Audit) and Stage 3 (Fact Verification) were run in external browser tools and returned by the operator. This supersedes the earlier Claude self-verification pass; the external review found real errors the self-check missed, which is exactly why the flagship dossier went through external review.

scores_returned.fc_derivation: Stage 3 factual_accuracy_score as returned; reflects the real errors found at review time, not re-inflated after correction

changes.field: concept three-numbers + tldr + mistake + fig-1 caption
changes.from: The second and third face no statutory limit at all.
changes.to: The hard 65% ceiling binds only statutory debt; total federal debt carries a softer 60% medium-term benchmark; only the all-in 84.1% figure has no aggregate statutory cap.
changes.reason: Both reviewers: the dossier claimed total federal debt faces 'no statutory limit' while elsewhere quoting Act 850's 60% benchmark on that exact measure. Self-contradiction and overclaim. Corrected across every place the claim appeared.

changes.from: ...it quietly swaps the capped number for the uncapped one, and reassures on the wrong basis.
changes.to: ...the number being reassured about is not the number the ceiling governs.
changes.reason: Stage 2 flagged 'quietly swaps' as conspiratorial framing attributing deliberate deception. Reworded to neutral statement of the mismatch.

changes.from: The IMF... noting that reaching 3% within five years is not assured. / 3% goal now targeted for 2028, two years past the original window.
changes.to: IMF baseline reaches 3% in 2028 with federal debt still ~61% in 2030, above the 60% target. / the 3% deficit is reached only in 2028.
changes.reason: Stage 3: IMF baseline actually reaches 3.0% in 2028; the 'not assured in five years' and 'two years past the original window' claims were unsupported. Replaced with the IMF's actual baseline numbers.

changes.from: RM424.7 billion in committed government guarantees... if every guarantee were called, debt could reach about 97%.
changes.to: RM424.7 billion in TOTAL guarantees, of which ~RM237B is committed... model a contingent-liability shock worth 15% of GDP and debt peaks near 97% in 2027.
changes.reason: Both reviewers: 'committed' conflated with 'total' (nearly doubling committed); and the 97% stress test assumes a 15%-of-GDP shock, not all guarantees being called. Both corrected.

changes.from: Public-private partnership commitments add a further RM112 billion. The largest single exposure is DanaInfra... followed by Prasarana... PTPTN.
changes.to: ...about RM153 billion in other obligations including PPPs. The largest guarantee exposures sit with infrastructure and financing vehicles such as DanaInfra and the public-sector housing and student-loan funds.
changes.reason: Stage 3: RM112B PPP figure not in primary tables (other liabilities are RM153.4B); exact DanaInfra/Prasarana/PTPTN ranking not verifiable. Used the verifiable aggregate and dropped the unverified ranking sequence.

changes.from: ...revised down toward RM2.5 to RM4 billion, with the World Bank publicly questioning even that.
changes.to: ...paired with the BUDI95 transfer that protects most motorists... projected to save around RM2.5 to RM4 billion... when global crude spiked in early 2026 the monthly subsidy bill climbed again.
changes.reason: Gemini: the World Bank/RM4B was misread (RM4B was a rising monthly COST due to oil prices, not a downgraded savings target) AND the card ignored BUDI95's social-protection role (economic masking). Both fixed; removed the unverified 'World Bank questioning' clause.

changes.from: RM26.4B (2020) to RM32B (2023)... 8.6% compound trend... log-linear fit RM98B to RM130B by 2040. Unfunded liability RM483B/RM800B/RM1.3T.
changes.to: MOF's own retirement charges RM35.9B (2024), RM40.1B (2025), RM42.8B (2026); govt projection RM46B (2030), RM120B (2040). Removed the specific unfunded-liability numbers; kept the unfunded/pay-as-you-go point.
changes.reason: Stage 3: the 2020-2023 series and the three liability estimates lacked a located primary source; and RM32B at 8.6% exceeds RM46B by 2030 (CAGR/projection inconsistency). Switched to MOF's primary retirement-charges figures; dropped the unverified liability specifics.

changes.from: In 2022 about 7.9 working-age adults... old-age dependency ratio rises from 12.6 to 21.7.
changes.to: Today around nine working-age adults stand behind each retiree... old-age dependency ratio roughly doubles by 2040 to about 21.7, leaving fewer than five.
changes.reason: Stage 3: DOSM 2022 implies ~9.5 (not 7.9), and the 12.6 OADR for 2022 was unsupported. Kept only the verified 2040 endpoint (21.7 -> ~4.6) and used a rounded, defensible 'today around nine'.

changes.from: It says nothing about total liabilities...
changes.to: It requires the fiscal outlook to report total debt and other liabilities, but sets no aggregate ceiling on them...
changes.reason: Stage 3: Act 850 does require reporting of total liabilities; the accurate criticism is the absence of a CAP, not silence. Reworded.

changes.from: 2009: statutory limit fixed at 55%; 2021 Temporary Measures Act sets 65%.
changes.to: Pre-2020: 55% self-imposed limit; 2020 Temporary Measures Act raises to 60%; 2021 raises to 65%.
changes.reason: Stage 3: the 55% was a pre-COVID self-imposed limit (not a 2009 statutory ceiling), and the Temporary Measures Act 2020 was the 55->60 step. Corrected the years and attributions.

charts_regenerated: fig-cover, fig-1, fig-3, fig-4 re-rendered to match corrected claims (fig-3 now labelled 'T4A illustration, not an official forecast' with soft endpoints; fig-4 uses MOF retirement-charges series; fig-1 shows 60% as benchmark; fig-cover stress-scenario wording). fig-2 unchanged (deficit actuals were verified).

rejected_or_noted_flags.flag: Stage 3: end-2025 figures (65.3% debt, 84.5% all-in) are newer than the end-June 2025 baseline
rejected_or_noted_flags.reason: The dossier's figures are correctly dated 'end-June 2025' and sourced to Fiscal Outlook 2026. Using a consistent, properly-dated vintage is correct; the end-2025 Fiscal Updates is a later release. The 'and growing' direction the dossier implies is in fact supported by the newer 84.5% number.

rejected_or_noted_flags.flag: Stage 2: subsidy framing ignores B40 impact
rejected_or_noted_flags.reason: Added the BUDI95 social-protection mechanism to the what-bends card. The dossier's lens is deliberately fiscal; full distributional analysis is out of scope for this edition but the protective mechanism is now acknowledged.

scores.note: Scores reflect the AS-REVIEWED state (real errors found). The corrections above resolve every actioned flag, but per pipeline convention the returned stage scores are recorded rather than re-inflated post-correction.

publish_recommendation: Corrections applied across cards, captions, and charts. Recommend re-running Stage 3 fact-check on the CORRECTED text before publishing, since the changes were substantial (a clean re-review would confirm the fixes and likely lift fc). At minimum, the dossier should not publish at the as-reviewed ba 55 / fc 72 without either a confirming re-review or the user's explicit acceptance. Stays published:false.
